allocatableMemoryMb.description: Memory workloads may be given: total minus what the host keeps for itself.

provisionedMemoryMb.description: Memory of every workload with compute, running or not.

runningMemoryMb.description: Memory of running workloads: what a start is admitted against.

DaemonView.description: The blocklyd process itself, as distinct from the node it runs on.

oneOf.description: Left in place; the workload is `retained` and a PUT brings its compute back.
Moved to the host's trash; purged after the retention (the last chance to undo).

existed.description: False when nothing by this id existed: a repeated delete is a no-op.

csrPem.description: PKCS#10, PEM. The key never leaves the node.

oneOf.description: It already matched; nothing was touched.
Made again for the new spec, keeping data and ports; started again if it was running.

exitCode.description: None when it timed out and was killed before reporting one.

killed.description:
blocklyd killed the process (by its host pid) after the timeout. Docker alone can't:
its API has no way to stop an exec (moby/moby#35703).

entries.description: Directories, files and links in the archive.

format.description: `tar.gz`: paths relative to the data root, like every archive Blockly keeps.

parts.description: Present when the archive went in parts: what finishes the upload.

sha256.description: Of the archive as uploaded: what a restore checks.

changed.description: False when this copy wasn't older than the current epoch, or was already fenced.

stopped.description: The copy was running and has been stopped.

certificateRenewedAt.description: When the node last renewed its certificates, in this run.

leaseRemainingSeconds.description:
How long this node may still restart a failed workload on its own (see
`fleet::heartbeat`). None until the control plane has granted a lease.

lifecycle.description: active, draining, lost or retired, as the control plane last said.

addresses.description: Where the node is reached now; the control plane follows a change.

reconciled.description: A full pass has looked since the runtime last didn't answer: the states below are current.

seq.description: Counts up within a session, so a late or replayed beat can be told apart.

sessionId.description:
New each time blocklyd starts. Two sessions beating for one node id at once are two
hosts with one identity.

upgradeFailed.description: An upgrade this node gave up on, going back to the binary it had (cli/upgrade.rs).

Issue.description: Something reconciliation or an operation found that the control plane should know about.

Locate.description: Where an operator finds it on the host. Informational; never a contract.

LogRecord.description: One line of `GET …/logs` (NDJSON): a log line, or the event that ends a stream.

oneOf.description: The copy shares the source's blocks until either changes: instant, and free until then.

NodeAddresses.description: Where the node is reached, as its configuration says now.

control.description: Where the control plane reaches console and status ports.

edge.description: Where the edge reaches game ports.

NodeCapacity.description:
Physical, reserved and allocated capacity, and what is actually used. Placement decides on
the control plane's own ledger; this is what the node sees, to check it against.

provisionedMemoryMb.description: Memory of every workload that holds compute here, running or not.

reflink.description: The data's filesystem shares blocks between copies: snapshots are nearly free.

runningMemoryMb.description: Memory of running workloads: what a start is admitted against.

snapshotBytes.description:
What local snapshots hold on the data disk, as their files count it (shared blocks are
counted in full, so it overstates what reflinked snapshots really take).

usedMemoryBytes.description:
The working set of running workloads, as the kernel counts it, from each one's latest
sample. A workload that runs but hasn't been sampled yet is left out; null only while
workloads run and none has been.

NodeFacts.description:
What the node says about itself when it joins. The control plane records it; the token, not
these facts, decides whether the node may join.

apiAddress.description: Where the control plane dials this node's API.

bootId.description: The kernel's boot id: a new one means the host rebooted.

edgeIps.description: Where the edge reaches game ports, and the control plane console and status ports.

machineIdSha256.description: sha256 of /etc/machine-id. Two nodes with the same one are clones of one image.

daemonVersion.description: blocklyd's version: what a control plane reads before relying on a feature.

fleet.description: In fleet mode: the control plane this node reports to, and when it last answered.

endpoints.description:
`host:port` per audience, `[v6]:port` for IPv6: where the edge and the control plane
reach this port. Blockly's `endpoint(handle, port, audience)`.

changed.description: False when it was already in the asked-for state: a repeat is a no-op, not an error.

forced.description: For stop: the workload didn't exit within the grace and was killed.

PutPart.description:
A part the node put: its number, from 1, and the ETag the store answered with, which the
control plane needs to finish the upload.

RenewRequest.description:
`POST /fleet/v1/nodes/{id}/renew`, over the node's current client certificate: a CSR for a new
key. The node keeps its id; only its certificates and key change.

cpuMillis.description:
CPU ceiling in thousandths of a core (CFS quota). Also what the JVM counts as its
processors. Absent: no ceiling, weight only.

cpuWeight.description: Share of CPU under contention, relative (cgroup weight). Absent: proportional to memory.

memoryMb.description: Hard memory limit (no swap). Blockly's size: 3072 for a 3 GB server.

pidsLimit.description: Processes and threads. Absent: the host default (4096).

previousData.description: Where the data it replaced went (the trash, for its retention).

sha256.description: The archive's, for a restore from a URL; none for a snapshot.

skipped.description: Links, devices and the like, which are never unpacked.

SnapshotId.description:
A local snapshot's id: the control plane's archive id (a UUID). It names a directory, so it is
held to a workload id's rules.

created.description: False when a snapshot with this id already existed; it is returned as it was made.

epoch.description: The epoch of the copy it was taken from.

quiesced.description: The workload was running, with its saving paused, when it was taken.

sizeBytes.description: The files' bytes. With shared blocks, most of them aren't new on disk.

cpuCores.description: Cores in use over the last sampling interval (1.0 = one full core).

memoryWorkingSetBytes.description: Usage minus inactive page cache: what the kernel would have to reclaim to fit.

WorkloadId.description:
What the control plane calls a workload: Blockly's server id (a UUID) in practice, but any
lowercase DNS label will do. The character set is the whole defence against path traversal
and injection: a valid id is always one safe path component, one safe container-name suffix
and one safe label value, so nothing downstream needs to escape it.

issues.description:
What the node found wrong with the workload and can't mend itself: a restart refused for
want of room, data over the size its spec promised. Left out when there is none.

WorkloadState.description:
What a workload is doing, normalized. How it maps onto Blockly's `ObservedState`:
created/stopped → stopped · running → running · stopping → stopping · crashed → crashed ·
restarting → starting (with `lastFailureAt`) · missing/retained → absent · creating → stopped
· unknown → unknown · fenced → stopped (this copy lost its placement; the current one is
elsewhere).

oneOf.description: Accepted; its container is being made.
Made and never started, or started again since.
A requested stop is in progress.
Exited after a requested stop, or on its own with code 0.
Exited on its own with a failure, or killed by the kernel for memory.
The host is starting it again after a failure (restart policy).
blocklyd holds a record but the container is gone (the runtime lost it).
Compute removed on request, data kept (`DELETE ?data=keep`).
The runtime can't be asked (Docker down).

Superseded: the control plane placed this workload anew (a newer epoch, usually on another
node). This copy is stopped, never started again, and its data kept until deleted.

changedAt.description: When the state last changed, as the runtime recorded it (survives blocklyd restarts).

epoch.description: The placement epoch this copy belongs to, if the control plane gave one.

generation.description: Bumped each time the container is made again for a new spec.

lastFailureAt.description: When it last failed and the host started it again (Blockly's `failedAt`).

restartCount.description:
Restarts the host made after failures since the last requested start or new spec. Kept
across restarts of blocklyd.

supersededBy.description: Set once a newer placement exists: the epoch that superseded this copy.
